context:
Patient: 59F, breast cancer survivor (2016: dose-dense AC, cumulative doxorubicin 240 mg/m2, left breast RT, on anastrozole), presents with left axillary mass, fevers to 38.4 C, drenching night sweats; ECOG 1, LDH 510. Non-GCB DLBCL (MYC 45%, BCL2 70%, FISH negative for rearrangements), PET nodes above and below the diaphragm plus splenic nodules, marrow negative, and new LVEF 45% (62% in 2016) with GLS -14%.
What this case tests: Spleen is a nodal site under Lugano, so stage is III, not IV, and IPI is 2. | Double-expressor by IHC but FISH-negative, so not double-hit; no intensification to DA-EPOCH-R. | Prior doxorubicin 240 mg/m2, left chest RT and LVEF 62% to 45% mean standard full-dose R-CHOP / Pola-R-CHP is not safe as is. | Treatment must stay curative: anthracycline-free (R-CEOP / R-GCVP) or cardio-protected regimen, with cardio-oncology input and cardioprotective drugs. | CNS-IPI 2 with no high-risk sites: no routine CNS prophylaxis.

answer.diagnosis: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, not otherwise specified (DLBCL, NOS), non-germinal-center B-cell-like (non-GCB/ABC-like) by the Hans algorithm (CD10 negative, BCL6 positive, MUM1/IRF4 positive), with a double-expressor immunophenotype (MYC about 45%, BCL2 about 70%) but no MYC, BCL2, or BCL6 rearrangement on FISH, so it is not a double-hit/triple-hit high-grade B-cell lymphoma. Ki-67 about 80%, EBER negative, CD5 negative. Metastatic breast carcinoma is excluded by morphology and by negative cytokeratin AE1/AE3 and GATA3 in the lesional cells. Ann Arbor/Lugano stage III with splenic involvement (IIIS); IPI 2.
answer.stage: Ann Arbor/Lugano stage III S: supradiaphragmatic left axillary and mediastinal (prevascular/left paratracheal) nodal disease, plus infradiaphragmatic mesenteric and para-aortic nodal disease and multiple FDG-avid splenic nodules. Bone marrow is negative and there is no non-lymphatic extranodal organ involvement (no liver, lung, bone, adrenal, kidney, or CNS disease), so this is stage III rather than IV. The largest mass is the 7.5 cm mesenteric conglomerate; it does not meet the NCCN >=10 cm definition of bulky disease. IPI 2 (stage III and elevated LDH; age 59, ECOG 1, no more than one extranodal site). CNS-IPI 2 (intermediate CNS risk, but no high-risk anatomic site).
answer.biology: Non-GCB/ABC-like DLBCL by Hans (CD10 negative, BCL6 positive, MUM1 positive in about 80%), with high proliferation (Ki-67 about 80%), BCL2 about 70% and MYC about 45% by IHC, meeting criteria for double-expressor lymphoma (MYC >=40%, BCL2 >=50%). FISH is negative for MYC (8q24), BCL2 (18q21), and BCL6 (3q27) rearrangements, so this is not double-hit/triple-hit and not a high-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC/BCL2 rearrangement. EBER is negative, CD5 is negative, and cyclin D1 is negative. The non-GCB/ABC and double-expressor phenotype is associated with inferior response to R-CHOP and is the rationale for considering Pola-R-CHP or novel agents, but the cardiac comorbidity constrains anthracycline use. No TP53 sequencing or gene-expression profiling is available.
answer.prognosis: Potentially curable with anthracycline-based immunochemotherapy, but the double-expressor/non-GCB biology and high Ki-67 place her at above-average risk of primary refractory or relapsed disease. IPI 2 is low-intermediate (original IPI 5-year OS about 50-60% in the CHOP era, better with rituximab), R-IPI 2 is 'good' (4-year PFS about 80%), and NCCN-IPI 2 is low-intermediate. I would quote a cure probability of roughly 60% (range about 50-70%), with the caveat that cardiac comorbidity may limit full-dose anthracycline delivery. Response to treatment is the strongest prognostic factor; a Deauville 4-5 end-of-treatment PET or primary progression would substantially worsen prognosis and prompt salvage/CAR-T planning.
answer.first_line_treatment: Curative intent: R-CHOP x6 cycles every 21 days (rituximab 375 mg/m2 IV day 1; cyclophosphamide 750 mg/m2 IV day 1; doxorubicin 50 mg/m2 IV day 1; vincristine 1.4 mg/m2 IV day 1, capped at 2 mg; prednisone 100 mg PO days 1-5). Because she has already received 240 mg/m2 doxorubicin and has an LVEF of 45% with GLS -14%, I would give dexrazoxane cardioprotection with each doxorubicin dose per label and co-manage with cardio-oncology. If cardio-oncology judges that any further anthracycline is unacceptable, or if LVEF falls further or she develops heart failure, I would switch to R-CEOP x6 (etoposide 100 mg/m2 IV days 1-3 replacing doxorubicin). I would not use Pola-R-CHP because it still contains doxorubicin and she has an LVEF of 45%; the pivotal POLARIX trial enrolled patients with preserved cardiac function, and this regimen would not address her main toxicity concern. No consolidation radiotherapy and no CNS-directed prophylaxis. Continue anastrozole to complete 10 years in November 2026; there is no clinically significant interaction with R-CHOP.
answer.cns_risk: CNS-IPI 2 (stage III and elevated LDH; age <60, ECOG 1, no more than one extranodal site, no kidney/adrenal involvement) = intermediate risk, approximately 4% 2-year risk (CNS-IPI low 0-1, intermediate 2-3, high 4-6). There is no testicular, breast, adrenal, kidney, epidural, or bone marrow involvement, and no CNS symptoms. I would not give intrathecal methotrexate or high-dose methotrexate and would not perform a diagnostic lumbar puncture. I would reassess if she develops neurologic symptoms, if the pathology is revised to a double-hit/high-grade lymphoma, or if a high-risk site (for example testis, breast, adrenal, kidney, or epidural) is found.
answer.response_assessment: Use Lugano 2014 criteria with FDG-PET/CT because the baseline disease is FDG-avid. I would not routinely do an interim PET after 2 cycles; if one is obtained, Deauville 1-3 does not alter the plan and Deauville 4-5 must be confirmed by biopsy because of false positives with rituximab. The key assessment is end-of-treatment FDG-PET/CT about 6-8 weeks (up to 12 weeks) after cycle 6: Deauville 1-3 = complete metabolic response; Deauville 4-5 = residual uptake requiring biopsy. Bone marrow was negative at baseline, so it does not need to be repeated. If end-of-treatment PET shows persistent disease, proceed to platinum-based salvage with or without rituximab and evaluate for CAR-T (axicabtagene ciloleucel, lisocabtagene maraleucel, or tisagenlecleucel) or autologous transplant. Reassess LVEF by echocardiogram before, during (after 2-3 cycles), and after therapy. If complete response, surveillance with history/exam and imaging only for symptoms; no consolidation radiation.
answer.pretreatment_workup: Already completed and adequate: excisional left axillary node biopsy with IHC and FISH; whole-body FDG PET-CT; bone marrow aspirate/biopsy (negative); CBC with differential, CMP, LDH, uric acid, beta-2 microglobulin, creatinine/eGFR; HIV, hepatitis B (HBsAg, anti-HBc, anti-HBs), and hepatitis C serologies; transthoracic echocardiogram; and ECOG performance status. Before starting therapy I would add: cardio-oncology consultation with baseline troponin/NT-proBNP and consideration of cardiac MRI if the echo is equivocal; obtain the prior breast radiotherapy records and estimate cardiac dose; optimize heart-failure therapy (ACE inhibitor/ARB and beta-blocker) and blood pressure; dental evaluation; document vaccination status and give inactivated influenza/pneumococcal/COVID vaccines before rituximab (live vaccines are contraindicated during and for at least 6 months after rituximab); baseline TSH, lipid panel, and HbA1c as part of cardiac risk assessment; and a hematopathology second review if there is any diagnostic uncertainty. Lumbar puncture and CNS imaging are not indicated. Pregnancy testing is not needed.
answer.supportive_care: Cardio-oncology: baseline and serial echocardiograms, troponin/NT-proBNP, guideline-directed heart-failure therapy (ACE inhibitor/ARB plus beta-blocker) and BP control, dexrazoxane with each doxorubicin dose, and careful fluid balance because of LVEF 45%. Antiemetics: 5-HT3 antagonist plus dexamethasone, with an NK1 antagonist and/or olanzapine for breakthrough; dexamethasone exposure is already part of R-CHOP. Primary G-CSF prophylaxis with pegfilgrastim 6 mg SC on day 2 (or equivalent filgrastim) because of the myelosuppressive regimen and her age/comorbidity; teach febrile-neutropenia precautions. Tumor lysis prophylaxis: allopurinol 300 mg daily (renal function is normal) with hydration and frequent uric acid/electrolyte/creatinine monitoring for at least the first cycle; rasburicase if uric acid rises or TLS develops, given the bulky mesenteric mass and high LDH. Infection: no routine PJP or antiviral prophylaxis for R-CHOP; consider TMP-SMX if prolonged corticosteroids are used; HBV antiviral prophylaxis is not needed because HBsAg and anti-HBc are negative, but she is anti-HBs negative and should be vaccinated when appropriate. VTE prophylaxis is not routine (Khorana score 1), but use LMWH if hospitalized or if additional risk. Constipation prophylaxis with vincristine (senna/laxatives), monitor for neuropathy. Steroid precautions: glucose and BP monitoring, sleep/mood support, bone protection with calcium/vitamin D. Continue anastrozole; maintain weight-bearing exercise and a healthy diet; psychosocial support and work accommodations; discuss hair loss; fertility is not relevant.
answer.fitness_and_goals: She is fit for curative-intent full-dose immunochemotherapy: 59 years old, ECOG 1, independent, working full time, no frailty, normal renal and hepatic function, and a supportive husband who drives her to visits. Her goals are cure and return to full-time work, which aligns with aggressive first-line therapy. The main vulnerability is cardiac: LVEF 45% (down from 62%), GLS -14%, prior doxorubicin 240 mg/m2, left breast radiotherapy, hypertension, and a family history of heart failure. I would explicitly discuss that the cardiac finding changes the regimen: R-CHOP will be given only with dexrazoxane cardioprotection, and R-CEOP is reserved for the situation where further anthracycline is judged unsafe. Cure remains the priority and can still be pursued. Shared decision-making should include the trade-off between the proven R-CHOP backbone and the less cardiotoxic but less well-studied R-CEOP, as well as the small risk of secondary malignancy and the planned completion of anastrozole. If she develops symptomatic heart failure or LVEF falls, the plan shifts to non-anthracycline therapy; if she remains fit and cardiac function is stable, complete 6 cycles and assess response. Code status and advance care planning are not documented but can be addressed later.
missing_information: Explicit Lugano/Ann Arbor stage documentation in a staged Condition resource (I derived stage III S from the PET/CT and bone marrow).
Cardio-oncology assessment and baseline cardiac biomarkers (troponin, NT-proBNP), plus consideration of cardiac MRI, given LVEF 45% and GLS -14%.
Prior left breast radiotherapy records with an estimate of cardiac radiation dose, and confirmation of the cumulative anthracycline dose (240 mg/m2 is documented).
Current cardiac medications and whether an ACE inhibitor/ARB and beta-blocker are tolerated; only amlodipine is listed.
Vaccination status (influenza, pneumococcal, COVID-19) and any prior live-vaccine exposure.
Hepatitis B vaccination status and any need for HBV DNA monitoring, since anti-HBs is nonreactive (HBsAg and anti-HBc are negative).
Baseline TSH, lipid panel, and HbA1c for cardiac risk assessment.
Patient preferences about alopecia, work schedule, and quality-of-life trade-offs, and insurance coverage for dexrazoxane or alternative regimens.
Whether anastrozole will be continued during chemotherapy (I recommend continuing; no significant interaction is documented).
Code status and advance care planning, and any distress/quality-of-life screening.
Expert hematopathology second opinion, TP53 sequencing, or gene-expression profiling (not standard, but would refine the double-expressor/non-GCB biology).

items.criterion: The response states the diagnosis is diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (NOS) with a non-germinal-center (non-GCB) phenotype by the Hans algorithm.
The response notes that Hans non-GCB is an immunohistochemical surrogate and is not equivalent to molecular ABC cell-of-origin by gene-expression profiling.
The response states the left axillary node is lymphoma and not recurrent breast carcinoma (cytokeratin AE1/AE3 and GATA3 negative).
The response stages the disease as Lugano/Ann Arbor stage III (nodes on both sides of the diaphragm with splenic involvement).
The response explains that the spleen is lymphatic tissue (a nodal site), so splenic nodules do not make the disease stage IV, and that there is no non-lymphatic extranodal or marrow involvement.
The response notes B symptoms (documented fevers >38 C and drenching night sweats).
The response notes the 7.5 cm mass is below the 10 cm Lugano bulk threshold, acknowledging that bulk definitions vary (some trials use 7.5 cm).
The response stages this patient as stage IV (e.g. by counting splenic involvement as extranodal disease).
The response classifies the lymphoma as double-expressor by IHC (MYC 45% >=40%, BCL2 70% >=50%) but NOT double-hit (FISH shows no MYC, BCL2 or BCL6 rearrangement).
The response classifies this lymphoma as double-hit / high-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements.
The response recommends DA-EPOCH-R (or another intensified regimen) on the basis of double-expressor biology.
The response calculates IPI as 2 (low-intermediate risk): elevated LDH and stage III; age 59, ECOG 1 and no extranodal sites (spleen is not counted as extranodal) score zero.
The response calculates CNS-IPI as 2 (intermediate risk).
The response states that routine CNS prophylaxis is not indicated (CNS-IPI 2, no kidney/adrenal, testicular or breast involvement).
The response mandates CNS prophylaxis (high-dose methotrexate or intrathecal therapy) for this patient.

The response recognizes anthracycline-related cardiac risk (prior doxorubicin 240 mg/m2, left chest radiotherapy, LVEF fall from 62% to 45%, i.e. cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction) and does NOT plan standard full-dose doxorubicin (R-CHOP or Pola-R-CHP) without first addressing cardiac function.

The response recommends standard R-CHOP or Pola-R-CHP (full-dose doxorubicin) without conditioning it on the reduced LVEF / prior anthracycline exposure (e.g. without cardio-oncology clearance, a cardioprotective modification, or a non-anthracycline alternative).
The response requests urgent cardio-oncology (or cardiology) evaluation before starting therapy.
The response starts or optimizes guideline-directed cardioprotective therapy: an ACE inhibitor/ARB (or ARNI) plus a beta-blocker (e.g. carvedilol), for example replacing amlodipine.

The response recommends a curative-intent anthracycline-free or anthracycline-modified regimen, e.g. R-CEOP (etoposide in place of doxorubicin) or R-GCVP; R-CHOP with liposomal doxorubicin or dexrazoxane is acceptable only if conditioned on cardio-oncology judging it safe.
The response acknowledges that anthracycline-free regimens likely have lower efficacy than anthracycline-based therapy.
The response plans serial cardiac monitoring during therapy: repeat LVEF/GLS imaging plus troponin and/or natriuretic peptide (BNP/NT-proBNP).
The response recommends palliative-only treatment, best supportive care, or hospice as the plan.
The response plans an end-of-treatment FDG PET-CT read with Lugano criteria / Deauville 5-point scale.
The response assesses tumor lysis risk as low-intermediate (normal creatinine and uric acid, LDH ~2x ULN) and gives allopurinol with hydration for cycle 1.
The response recommends (or reasonably considers) primary G-CSF support with each cycle.
The response addresses the ongoing anastrozole: continuing it is acceptable (no meaningful interaction), or holding it in coordination with breast oncology is also acceptable.
The response confirms hepatitis B serology was checked (HBsAg and anti-HBc nonreactive) before rituximab.
The response judges the patient fit for curative-intent therapy (ECOG 1, normal organ function apart from the LVEF) and acknowledges her goal of cure.
The response lists the cause of the LVEF decline / cardio-oncology work-up as missing (e.g. ischemic evaluation given prior left chest radiotherapy, cardiac MRI, baseline troponin and NT-proBNP).
